title: Jastrow v2 entry
description: One entry of Jastrow’s dictionary at schemaVersion 2 (headword design §2). Generated from admin/entry/schema.ts by bun schema:build; never edit this file by hand.

schemaVersion.description: The entry-file format version. 2 is the headword-design §2 shape, ruled 2026-09-21; 3 drops the superscript disambiguator and formerNames (ruling 11-13 url words). Stamped on every file so a reader can tell the versions apart without inferring it from which keys are present.

id.description: The rid, which the entry is addressed by. The name is not stored: it is derived from headwords[0], so it cannot drift from the headword (URL names spec §5.1).

sefariaHeadword.description: Sefaria's headword for this rid, byte for byte (URL names spec §5.1, U3). Import is the only writer.

headwords.description: Every form print sets on the headword line, in its order. headwords[0] is the primary form: the name, the search key and every link derive from it (headword design §2).

display.description: How print laid the headword line out: a template whose {n} inserts headwords[n].text and whose every other character is literal notation, never Hebrew (headword design §2, §3.1). It never carries Sefaria's superscript: print sets none (ruling 11-13 url words). Optional and never defaulted — where the source cannot settle the layout the key is absent and the row is flagged (§3).

page.description: Where print sets this entry: page, and column a or b. The entry file is the record (ruling 11-05 page index).

pos.description: Part of speech. Declared, with no producer: no entry carries it (docs/ideas.md, Schema).

stem.description: The stem label print gives (Pa., Hithpa., …).

forms.description: The headword forms this stem governs.

items.description: A binyan section of a written entry. Sibling to the entry's own senses, so both can be present on one entry.

field.description: Which field of its object: text or homograph on a form; gloss, label or units[n] on a sense.

kind.description: print-error (case 2, corrected), kept (case 3, kept as printed, so printed equals stored) or illegible (case 4, our best reading).

printed.description: Print's reading of the field; '' where print sets nothing. A homograph is written as print writes it (I), a label as its token without ) (5).

stored.description: What the field holds. For gloss and units[n], the substring the note is about.

evidence.description: Case 2: the proof. Case 3: the readings. Case 4: why.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the print read or the ruling.

annotation.description: One departure from print, or one print reading checked and kept, on the object whose field it describes (admin/entry/ANNOTATIONS.md §2; ruling 10-13 correction policy). printed is print's reading ('' where print sets nothing), stored what the field holds (for gloss and units[n], the substring the note is about). kind: print-error (case 2), kept (case 3: printed equals stored), illegible (case 4). source is the patch that wrote it. What the schema cannot express — the field resolves on its object, stored agrees with the field, kept iff printed equals stored, one annotation per field, a real calendar date — admin/entry/annotations.ts enforces.

annotations.description: Absent when there are none, never [].

text.description: The form as clean Hebrew: meaning only. Everything print sets around the forms lives in the entry’s display.

homograph.description: The Roman numeral beside this form, as a number. Part of the name, and always shown in display. Print sets it, or (ruling 10-13 correction policy) Jastrow's own text names it and a homograph annotation says so.

reconstructed.description: Print stars this form as a reconstructed word (headword design §3.1 rule 3). Only ever true.

gender.description: This form's gender label, as print sets it beside the form (headword design §4). An entry carries at most one of a per-form gender on EVERY headword or a grammar.gender, never both, and neither is inherited (ruling HW-gender). This schema cannot express it; admin/entry/validate.ts enforces it.

partial.description: This form is shown exactly as printed and is never a lookup key (headword design §2): an ending after an ellipsis, or a phrase holding an abbreviated word. Only ever true.

formObject.description: One headword form. It holds only meaning; how print sets the forms around each other is the entry’s display (headword design §2, §3.1).

reconstructed.description: Print stars this sense's number (*2)), as it stars a reconstructed headword form (ruling 10-04 sense star). Only ever true, and only beside a label. The dash print sets before a later sense is not stored.

gloss.description: The sense's own head text. On the entry's senses[0] it is the lead text, usually the whole definition (ruling 10-04 lead text).

units.description: The sense's numbered or lettered parts.

sense.description: One sense of a written entry. Every label is an explicit string, so a reader that drops an empty lead renumbers nothing (ruling 10-04 lead text).
